thread:
Nora Chen: Quick accessibility note from the dashboard filters review: selected filter chips (compact mode) use a 1px highlight that disappears at certain zoom levels. Keyboard users can't tell which chip is active. Screenshot: https://redwood-internal/short/filters-zoom.png :mag:
Ben Ortiz: Repro'd. Also the chips are role=button but we don't use aria-pressed, so SR doesn't announce selected state.
Sasha Lee: For toggle chips use aria-pressed="true|false" or role="switch" depending on semantics. Also ensure the focus indicator is at least 3px and meets 3:1 contrast with the background.
Nora Chen: Proposed CSS for focus ring:
```css
.chip:focus { outline: 3px solid var(--focus-accent); outline-offset: 2px; }
.chip--selected { background: var(--chip-selected-bg); color: var(--chip-selected-fg); }
```
But need to pick --focus-accent that contrasts with both light and dark chip-selected colors.
Ben Ortiz: Could use a dual-layer approach: a solid inner ring + translucent outer glow to work on both themes. Eg: box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(0,95,204,0.16); outline: 3px solid #005fcc; test contrast.
Sasha Lee: Also important: chips are in a horizontal scroll region. When tabbing, focus jumps but doesn't scroll the chip into view consistently. We should call element.scrollIntoView({block:'nearest', inline:'nearest'}) on focus.
Nora Chen: Good call. And the keyboard order currently goes: input -> chips -> Apply button. But when chips overflow, tabbing can skip chips that are offscreen. We must ensure all chips are tabbable in DOM order even if visually offscreen. No aria-hidden on overflowed chips.
Ben Ortiz: For screen readers, add aria-live="polite" on the filter summary that says "3 filters applied" when selection changes. Keep updates debounced 300ms to avoid spam.
Sasha Lee: Also add role="listbox" on the chip container and role="option" on each chip if treating as multi-select listbox; then manage aria-selected on each. That gives SRs consistent semantics. If we keep them as buttons, aria-pressed is fine. Choose one pattern and document it.
Nora Chen: Plan: 1) pick listbox+option pattern for keyboard selection and arrow-key roving; 2) implement focus scrollIntoView on focus; 3) stronger focus token and theme-contrast check; 4) aria-live summary with debounce; 5) Playwright test: keyboard arrow navigation across chips, tab to Apply, assert summary updates.
Maya Patel: Small copy nit: summary text should read "3 filters applied, 12 results" not "3 filters applied (12)" so SR reads naturally. Also include the filter names in the summary for quick context.
a11y-bot: Auto-scan: chip focus outline contrast 2.1:1 \u26a0\ufe0f; aria-pressed missing on .chip role=button \u274c; focus-in-scroll behavior inconsistent \u26a0\ufe0f; aria-live absent for filter summary \u274c. Report: https://redwood-internal/a11y/2104567890
Ben Ortiz: I'll put a small PR with the listbox pattern, JS for roving tabindex + scrollIntoView, and the aria-live summary debounce. Will include screenshots for light/dark/high-contrast.
Sasha Lee: When you open the PR include manual VoiceOver/NVDA steps and a short demo GIF of keyboard navigation. Also tag @eng-runtime if scrollIntoView triggers any layout jank we need to mitigate.
Nora Chen: Thanks — will open PR today and assign for design review. :white_check_mark:
